correctness.rationale: A face with at least three vertices can neither contain the center nor repeat an arm; a center-free partial transversal is always a face. This gives the r-fold join of the L depth labels and precisely the stated extra one-cells. The join orbit space is the sorted-weight chamber: sorting is continuous and the compact quotient maps bijectively into a Hausdorff polyhedron. Adding the other weights of a depth to its largest while scaling those others down preserves the simplex sum and never increases the total number of occupied slots. It fixes the section with one slot per depth and retracts onto the simplex skeleton. The one-pivot Morse matching on the skeleton is acyclic because all possible downward covers deleting the pivot with nonempty lower face are reversed; it has one critical vertex and exactly binom(L−1,r) critical top faces. This count is zero for L≤r, first becomes one at L=r+1, and is separated from degree one by r≥3. Edge stabilizers cannot exchange distinct depths or exchange the center with an arm vertex. Consequently the extra edges are intervals attached at their stated vertices, with one central edge a contractible attachment and the others contributing the asserted loops. For L=1 this adds no loop. The barycentric flag computations recorded at four primes are corroborative and were not replayed; the deformation, matching, and attachments prove the integral statement.

evidence: Apply the published one-label step to each depth in succession. At any stage a partially coalesced space is a compact polyhedron: in sorted slot coordinates it is a finite union of polytopes indexed by occupied slot patterns, with already merged labels allowed at most one occupied slot. When merging the next label, fix the weights of all other labels. If they occupy k slots and the new label has total mass s>0, the fiber is exactly s_1≥…≥s_(r−k)≥0 with sum s, a simplex. At zero mass it is a point. The cell-like comparison used in the cited proof therefore gives a homotopy equivalence at each step, without assuming D is connected.

The total merge has the simplicial depth skeleton as a section. Its inclusion is a homotopy equivalence since the merge is one, and is a cofibration since it is a subpolyhedron. A cofibration that is a homotopy equivalence admits a strong deformation retraction onto its image, hence fixes all attaching vertices. The known face decomposition now gives exactly one orbit interval per distinct depth pair and L central intervals, the first of which attaches the center contractibly. The simplex skeleton wedge is standard.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Thus both the existence of the asserted strong deformation retraction and the full quotient type follow by repeating an already published topological operation and attaching the known extra edges. The new displayed linear homotopy is a direct coordinate realization of this merge; it does not change the claimed invariant or introduce a new obstruction or scope.
